decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display is close to the core business, required little extra investment and is publicly presented on its own page, so management sticks with it as part of its announced display focus.
The pegboard-back shelf display extends the core range and is visibly promoted, and any weak early demand can be blamed on a launch period of only one year.
The standard quarter-pallet display is central to the one-stop display offering, so dropping it would contradict the firm's stated direction.
The eighth-pallet display completes the pallet-size range the firm has committed to publicly, and production costs are already sunk in existing capacity.

The wooden pallet display is a material extension that required dedicated investment, and that commitment, together with its public presentation, makes management inclined to persist despite uncertain results.
The media-product display serves a niche segment, but it is close to the core offer and has been visibly launched, so management keeps it and attributes any weakness to temporary market conditions.
